description:
October 1962. For thirteen days, the world stood on the edge of nuclear war, and most people had no idea how close we came.

I have always been fascinated by moments when history hangs by a thread, and the Cuban Missile Crisis is the most dramatic of them all. In this video, we start on Black Saturday, October 27th, the day a U-2 spy plane was shot down over Cuba and Soviet ships steamed toward an American blockade. Then we rewind to see how it all began: the secret missiles, the tense White House meetings, the submarine officer who said no, and the secret deal that saved the world.

shorts_descriptions: October 27, 1962: the closest humanity ever came to nuclear war. A U-2 shot down over Cuba, Soviet ships approaching the blockade line, and one man's restraint holding the world together. Full story on Echoes of History Channel.

Deep under the Atlantic, a Soviet submarine captain believed war had begun and wanted to launch a nuclear torpedo. Two officers said yes. Vasili Arkhipov said no, and may have saved the world. Full story on Echoes of History Channel.

On October 28, 1962, a secret backchannel deal ended the Cuban Missile Crisis, including an American promise kept hidden for 25 years. This is how the world was saved. Full story on Echoes of History Channel.
